newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Fredriksen plans to buy LOFS - report.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Fredriksen plans to buy LOFS - report.

text.p: Norwegian shipowner John Fredriksen plans to take over Bermuda-registered tanker company London & Overseas Freighters Plc, the daily financial Dagens Naeringsliv (DN) said on Friday.
The newspaper said Fredriksen, the major shareholder in Swedish shipping company Frontline AB, planned to merge LOFS with the Stockholm-listed group.
Director Tor Olav Troeim in Fredriksen's company Seatankers declined to comment, DN said.
LOFS operates six tankers, three 150,000 tonne Suezmax vessels built in 1993 and 1995 and three 14- to 15-year-old 62,000 tonne Panamax ships.
In February 1997 LOFS announced it was exploring strategic alternatives designed at repositioning the company to compete more effectively and enhance shareholder value.
Sources said a number of companies have expressed an interest in LOFS, but no decision is expected for six to eight weeks.
However, shipping analysts have expressed doubts about the outcome - with some claiming that LOFS has overvalued its assets by 5 percent. The company has valued its fleet at $219.8 million.
DN said LOFS Suezmax tankers would make a good fit with Frontline, which is in the process of building up its tanker fleet.
